summary: Computers, Ethernet, NMEA 0183 and NMEA 2000 networks, and the bridge instruments they link.

blocks.title: The BIOS
items: BIOS, basic input-output system: a small program in a chip that starts the computer. Its 4 main functions: P.O.S.T., bootstrap loader, BIOS drivers, BIOS setup.

blocks.title: PC fixes
items: Power on, won't boot: use BIOS setup mode to check settings, such as boot device order.
XP drive types: Start, Programs, Accessories, System Information.
New CD-ROM drive: same interface system as the old one.

blocks.title: Ethernet and routers
items: A LAN, local area network, links devices called nodes.
Ethernet is a star: each node's home run cable goes back to the central hub.
Collision domain: only 1 node sends at a time; all share the bandwidth.
10Base-T, 100Base-TX: megabits per second, T for twisted pair. Cable: CAT-5 with 4 twisted pairs.
USB 2.0 cable: 5 meters max.
Router: links networks. Exam addresses: 192.168.1.1, 192.168.0.1, 192.168.2.0.
Installing one: open a web browser, enter the router's address, then username and password.

blocks.title: NMEA basics
items: NMEA, National Marine Electronics Association: a talker sends text sentences; listeners receive.
Ground loop: a shield grounded at both ends adds noise and data errors.

blocks.title: Bridge instruments
items: Depth finder: echo time × 1500 m/s ÷ 2 = depth. 200-400 kHz, pulses 25 to 600 µs.
Gyro compass finds true north. Older ones: carbon pile for voltage regulation.
Fiber-optic gyro: 3 fiber-optic coils and a dual-axis electronic level sensor.
SSAS, Ship Security Alert System: a covert alert via Inmarsat-C to specific addresses, never an all ships alert. No alarm aboard.
AIS, Automatic Identification System, broadcasts identity, position, course and speed on VHF 87B (161.975 MHz), 88B (162.025 MHz), 9.6 kbs GMSK.
Electronic chart system inputs: position, speed, depth, radar. ECDIS, Electronic Chart Display and Information System, is the approved kind.
C-Map charts: license information for each computer.
Auto pilot needs course information and rudder feedback, from a rudder feedback unit. GPS isn't necessary.
VDR, Vessel Data Recorder, the black box, records position, speed, heading, depth, radar, bridge audio and VHF. CSM keeps up to 12 hours; DAU as long as 30 days.

blocks.title: Exam traps
items: BIOS functions never include printer drivers, CPU or RAM setup.
NMEA 2000 speed: pick 250 bps, though it really runs at 250 kilobits.
Multiplexers, combiners, routers aren't NMEA 2000 parts.
Wrong chart input list: radar, SSAS and position.
VDR: any list with EGC data or MSI is wrong.
